risks_observed: The strong return here offset losses in YELP and BKNG at the basket level, but that offset was coincidental rather than structural — the strategy has no mechanism to size up into higher-conviction names or correlate position sizing with prior-day move magnitude.

thesis: Strongest candidate by both 5d (+1.79%) and 20d (+6.28%) relative strength, above rising SMA20 and SMA50, RSI 62.5 not overbought. The macro energy supply-shock thesis (USO elevated, XLE ranked #1 sector) provides direct tailwind with no reversal signal — yesterday's +0.47% was a low-volume day and the trend structure is intact heading into day 2.
outcome_notes: Trade closed at schedule with a clean 2.35% gain, confirming the trend continuation thesis. Price action followed through on the energy supply-shock tailwind without needing the stop as a backstop — the scheduled exit captured the move without overstaying.
risks_observed: Single-sector concentration in energy means the gain is tightly correlated with USO/XLE sentiment; a reversal in crude overnight would have unwound this quickly. No trailing stop meant the full position was exposed to any intraday spike-and-reverse that happened to close near entry.

thesis: Second-best performer in the candidate set (5d +2.38%, 20d +4.12%), above both SMAs, consistent with the mildly bullish XLV healthcare view as a defensive rotation leg. Tighter stop than energy to limit downside after yesterday's modest loss; 1-day horizon keeps cost gate achievable.
outcome_notes: Healthcare leg gave back ground despite the defensive-rotation rationale, with price drifting below entry and closing with a modest loss. The 5d and 20d momentum that justified the entry did not translate into day-of follow-through, suggesting relative strength was already fading at entry.
risks_observed: Pairing a weakening healthcare position against a strong energy position in the same basket creates correlation risk in reverse — if energy had also underperformed, the session loss would have been material. The tighter stop intended to limit downside was not tight enough to avoid the loss, indicating the stop sizing may not be calibrated to recent EXH1.DE volatility.

thesis: Q1 earnings beat (sales €1.94B vs €1.80B, net income up) combined with today's fresh institutional analysis coverage keeps the reaction developing; RSI at 38.8 after a 20-day correction leaves substantial room before overbought conditions, and the FX-only cost structure (0.30% round-trip) gives favourable risk/reward versus LSE names.
outcome_notes: Price advanced steadily through the session with no significant reversal, consistent with institutional re-rating continuing after the earnings print. The scheduled exit captured the move cleanly; the low RSI at entry gave enough technical runway for the thesis to develop without hitting resistance.
risks_observed: EUR-denominated exposure creates unhedged FX drag for a GBP-reporting book that isn't reflected in the gross move. Defence names can gap on geopolitical headlines intraday — holding to a scheduled exit rather than a trailing stop left the full gain exposed to a late-session reversal that didn't materialise but easily could have.

thesis: Dr. Martens reported a return to profit growth in FY2026 — the first earnings inflection after a prolonged downturn — with full-price selling discipline that institutional models will reward; RSI at 56.5 and both SMAs now supportive suggest the reaction still has a session of follow-through.
outcome_notes: Price drifted up one tick over the session, suggesting the institutional re-rating is real but slow-moving rather than momentum-driven. The scheduled exit captured the drift, though the thin absolute move on a sub-penny spread stock implies liquidity was not deep enough to express the thesis at meaningful size.
risks_observed: At this price level, bid-ask spread costs are a disproportionately large fraction of realised gain, and any slippage on exit would have eroded the position materially. The stock's extended prior downtrend means overhead supply from stranded holders is a persistent drag that a single earnings print may not clear quickly.

thesis: Cranswick's FY profit jumped ~18% on 9.5% revenue growth and the company is accelerating capex — a confidence signal that typically attracts quality-focused buyers in a risk-off session where defensive food outperforms; RSI 62.4 and above both SMAs confirm the trend.
outcome_notes: Price declined through the session despite the strong earnings backdrop, indicating the beat was already priced in or that broader sector selling outweighed the fundamental catalyst. The scheduled exit provided no protection, absorbing the full intraday move against the position.
risks_observed: Entering with RSI at 62.4 left almost no technical buffer — the stock was already extended before the session opened, making it vulnerable to profit-taking on any softening. Running CWK.L alongside DOCS.L created implicit UK consumer-sector correlation in the day's basket; a risk-off rotation or sector-wide sell hit both names and there was no offset.

thesis: 2.3 ATRs below 20d SMA with no identifiable news catalyst is the strongest ATR-extension signal in today's list; RSI 30.3 is borderline but the extension alone justifies a small bet on mean reversion — kept small given thin volume (0.02 ratio) which could limit intraday liquidity.
outcome_notes: Price recovered toward the 20d SMA as expected, validating the ATR-extension read — no news catalyst meant the dip was purely technical and buyers stepped in intraday. Exit was scheduled rather than thesis-driven, so the position was closed while reversion was still in progress rather than at natural mean exhaustion.
risks_observed: The 0.02 volume ratio flagged at entry was the live risk: a scheduled exit on a thin name can widen spreads at an arbitrary time rather than when liquidity is best, compressing realised gain. RSI at 30.3 was marginal — not deeply oversold — so the reversion had limited momentum behind it and a single down-tick session could have negated the extension signal before the scheduled close.

thesis: Iran war premium is firmly embedded — no diplomatic progress (talks stalled, US seized an Iranian tanker intraday) and a 9.1M barrel API crude draw against a 3.4M est confirms physical tightness on both the geopolitical and fundamental axes. Technicals support continuation: RSI 64.8, MACD positive, price 8.4% above SMA20; 1-day hold keeps the position clear of overnight diplomatic headline risk.
outcome_notes: Price moved against the position immediately and hit the stop, suggesting the geopolitical premium was already priced in at entry or unwound intraday — the API draw failed to sustain the bid. The thesis required continued momentum; instead the market faded, likely on profit-taking or a softening of the Iran headline after the tanker seizure was digested.
risks_observed: The entry was chasing an already-extended move (8.4% above SMA20, RSI near overbought territory), leaving little cushion if sentiment reversed on any diplomatic noise or a weaker-than-expected prompt spread. Geopolitical premium trades carry binary headline risk that a 1-day hold does not fully avoid — a partial de-escalation signal intraday was sufficient to collapse the thesis before the stop could be managed.

thesis: Top previous-day gainer (+18.38% close-to-open). Rule-based control: buying the prior session's strongest movers with no further filter.
outcome_notes: Price went nowhere on the day — the prior session's +18.38% gap was fully absorbed at the open and intraday buyers showed no follow-through. The loss is effectively spread/slippage rather than directional movement, but the thesis (momentum continuation) did not hold for this name.
risks_observed: GLEN is a commodity miner, making it the most macro-sensitive name in the basket; a gap this large in a cyclical often signals exhaustion rather than continuation. No intraday stop meant the strategy held through any dip for zero gain, and the flat close confirms that holding the position all day added no edge over simply not entering.

thesis: Top previous-day gainer (+16.90% close-to-open). Rule-based control: buying the prior session's strongest movers with no further filter.
outcome_notes: Price drifted steadily higher through the session and held gains into the scheduled close, suggesting the prior-day catalyst (likely a clinical or commercial announcement) sustained genuine buy-side interest rather than speculative gap-chasing. The +1.12% intraday move on top of a large prior gap is a cleaner continuation signal than the other names.
risks_observed: AZN is a large-cap pharma where single-day moves of this magnitude are nearly always news-specific; without knowing the catalyst, the strategy cannot distinguish a sustained re-rating from a gap that will mean-revert over the following days. A positive outcome here does not validate the rule — it reflects surviving an unknown fundamental driver.

thesis: Top previous-day gainer (+16.38% close-to-open). Rule-based control: buying the prior session's strongest movers with no further filter.
outcome_notes: ULVR ground modestly higher through the day and exited near the session high, consistent with a defensive consumer-staples name retaining a prior gap rather than reversing it. The continuation was orderly rather than momentum-driven.
risks_observed: A +16.38% prior gap in a slow-moving staples stock is an unusual event and likely catalyst-specific; the intraday continuation could just as easily have been a mean-reversion setup. The strategy holds no mechanism to distinguish between the two regimes at entry.

thesis: Top previous-day gainer (+14.79% close-to-open). Rule-based control: buying the prior session's strongest movers with no further filter.
outcome_notes: SPX.L produced the second-largest intraday gain in the basket despite having the smallest prior-day gap, suggesting relative price strength was still building on the day rather than exhausted at the open. The scheduled exit captured that continuation cleanly.
risks_observed: Four of five positions exited green and the basket is entirely UK-listed — a broad FTSE risk-off event intraday would have correlated all names downward simultaneously with no stop in place. The strategy's only exit gate is end-of-day, leaving full intraday drawdown exposure uncapped.

thesis: Top previous-day gainer (+13.90% close-to-open). Rule-based control: buying the prior session's strongest movers with no further filter.
outcome_notes: BA.L was the strongest performer on the day and the prior gap-up in a defence name likely reflected a news catalyst (contract award or geopolitical newsflow) with enough fundamental weight to sustain buying interest through the session. The exit at the high of the quoted range suggests price was still bid at the close.
risks_observed: Defence stocks can reverse sharply on headline risk (ceasefires, budget cuts, contract cancellations) intraday with no warning — the absence of a trailing stop or news-aware exit means the strategy is fully exposed to that binary outcome. Today's result is correct, but the payoff structure is asymmetric without a protective layer.

thesis: Energy supply shock thesis is intact and accelerating — oil above $103 on Iran impasse with no diplomatic resolution visible, MACD histogram strongly positive (+0.395), above both SMAs, #1 sector by 5d (+6.46%) and 20d (+9.70%); holding 2 days as the catalyst is structural, not single-session.
outcome_notes: The Iran truce — the same macro event cited as bullish for XLF in the same basket — directly invalidated the supply-shock catalyst here, pulling oil off $103 and triggering the stop. Price action offered no support as the structural driver reversed intraday, and the stop executed as designed with no overshoot to flag.
risks_observed: The basket held XLE (long Iran impasse) and XLF (long Iran truce) simultaneously, creating an internally contradictory book where one leg was guaranteed to be wrong on the geopolitical outcome. Single-catalyst event risk with no hedge: once the catalyst flipped, there was no secondary thesis to slow the drawdown to the stop level.

thesis: Defensive rotation bid reinforced by today's 30Y spike to 19-year highs; XLP sits above both SMAs with MACD histogram positive, #2 sector on both 5d and 20d — risk-off tape is the catalyst.
outcome_notes: Price barely moved — the 0.06% gross gain was fully consumed by execution costs, producing a net loss despite the directional thesis being directionally correct. The risk-off bid materialised but lacked enough follow-through within the holding window to generate a meaningful price move; the scheduled exit captured nothing beyond noise.
risks_observed: The 30Y spike thesis was macro-level and slow-moving — XLP as a bond-proxy proxy is susceptible to intraday mean-reversion even when the multi-day trend is intact, making a same-day scheduled exit a poor fit for the catalyst type. Holding alongside XLV created a correlated defensive basket; if the tape had reversed, both positions would have bled simultaneously with no natural hedge.

thesis: Healthcare is the non-bond-proxy defensive — no 30Y structural headwind unlike XLU/XLRE — with MACD histogram inflecting sharply upward and above-average volume (1.28x) consistent with quality rotation inflows.
outcome_notes: The MACD inflection and volume signal didn't translate into price discovery within the session — the one-cent gain shows the market absorbed the inflow without producing a directional move. Scheduled exit left no room for the quality-rotation thesis to develop over the timeframe it actually needed.
risks_observed: Running two defensive-sector longs simultaneously (XLP + XLV) on the same macro day concentrated the book in a single factor bet — a sentiment shift away from defensives would have hit both legs. The above-average volume read could reflect distribution rather than accumulation; without confirming price expansion, it's an ambiguous signal that the strategy accepted at face value.

thesis: Cisco's May 13 Q3 earnings beat (paired with restructuring discipline in item 2.05) continues to attract buyers, and today's Rosenblatt $150 price target with 30% upside framing adds fresh institutional momentum to the one tech sub-sector (networking/AI infrastructure) holding up against bond-repricing headwinds. Exit before NVDA earnings tomorrow to avoid sector-wide sympathy volatility.

Goldman Sachs raises PT to $57 this morning while price holds above both MAs with RSI 63.5 and MACD histogram +1.792 — strongest momentum setup in the candidate set with a fresh analyst catalyst aligning with energy sector tailwinds.
outcome_notes: The GS price-target raise acted as a genuine catalyst — price moved directly toward take-profit with no meaningful retracement, suggesting the upgrade attracted fresh institutional buying rather than just triggering a momentary spike. RSI at entry (63.5) left enough room before overbought territory for the move to develop cleanly, and the MACD histogram strength confirmed momentum was not already exhausted.
risks_observed: ENPH carries substantial policy sensitivity as a solar name — an adverse rate or subsidy headline mid-session could have reversed the catalyst effect before take-profit was reached. Single-analyst-upgrade setups are also prone to fast fading if the broader energy sector stalled; the trade had no fundamental floor below the technical support levels.

thesis: 20d +37.64% trend intact with price above both MAs, but RSI 74.2 and decelerating MACD histogram (+0.219) limit conviction — tight stop to exit quickly if the momentum stalls.
outcome_notes: Price pushed through to take-profit despite entering with a nearly exhausted momentum signal — the 20-day trend's underlying strength was sufficient to overcome the RSI overextension and the near-flat MACD histogram. The tight-stop protective design proved unnecessary, but the trade's success was more attributable to trend persistence than to entry-point quality.
risks_observed: An RSI of 74.2 at entry meant almost no buffer before a reversal would have looked technically justified to other participants; a single risk-off hour could have swept the tight stop for a loss on what resolved as a winner. The decelerating histogram was a real warning sign that the best of the move may already have been captured by prior holders, leaving this entry exposed to a mean-reversion snapback with little margin for error.

thesis: IRGC explicitly threatening to extend the Iran war beyond the region and live supertanker disruptions at Hormuz are same-day operational escalation catalysts, not priced-in rumor — this is the cleanest fresh geopolitical catalyst since the supply shock began. Technicals confirm: above SMA20/50, RSI 60.8, MACD histogram positive, strongest sector by a wide margin with the 9.1M barrel inventory draw adding fundamental support.
outcome_notes: Price reversed sharply from entry and the stop triggered at $143.50, a ~4% drawdown. The geopolitical catalyst — IRGC threats and live Hormuz disruptions — failed to sustain a bid, suggesting the market had already front-run the supply-shock narrative or that macro risk-off (dollar strength, demand-side pressure) overwhelmed the headline. Technicals were bullish at entry but offered no cushion once the move went the wrong way.
risks_observed: Geopolitical momentum entries carry a built-in 'buy the rumor, sell the fact' trap — by the time a catalyst is clean enough to act on, it's often partially priced. USO also introduces roll drag and tracking error that compounds losses relative to spot crude. With a single commodity, single-leg position and no correlated hedge (e.g. long refiners or short tanker shorts), the basket had zero offset when the thesis failed.

thesis: Top previous-day gainer (+12.73% close-to-open). Rule-based control: buying the prior session's strongest movers with no further filter.
outcome_notes: LPG extended its prior-day move cleanly through the session, adding another 7.5% before the scheduled close — the momentum catalyst (likely a shipping/freight rate move) had legs beyond the gap. Holding to a fixed scheduled exit captured the full intraday trend without needing any active management.
risks_observed: Entering after a 12.73% gap meant buying at a significantly extended level; a gap-fill reversal would have produced a sharp loss with no stop in place to limit it. Scheduled-only exit is a missing safety net that worked here but represents a structural vulnerability across every name in this basket.

thesis: Top previous-day gainer (+10.57% close-to-open). Rule-based control: buying the prior session's strongest movers with no further filter.
outcome_notes: RXO was the standout of the basket, adding over 11% intraday on top of its prior-day gap — sustained buying pressure suggests the catalyst (likely a freight volume or earnings revision) was being re-rated across the session rather than fading. The scheduled exit captured most of the move.
risks_observed: RXO is a freight brokerage name with high beta to macro transport sentiment; any negative headline mid-session (e.g., rate cut expectations shifting, fuel cost spike) could have reversed this quickly with no downside protection. The 11%+ gain also means significant mark-to-market risk was carried intraday without a trailing stop.

thesis: Top previous-day gainer (+9.43% close-to-open). Rule-based control: buying the prior session's strongest movers with no further filter.
outcome_notes: IPGP moved modestly positive but well below what the prior-day gap implied — the intraday price action was tepid, suggesting the catalyst was already priced in by the open and buyers were thin for the remainder of the session.
risks_observed: IPGP and LSCC both sit in the semiconductor space, creating unintended sector concentration in a two-name correlated pair within a five-stock basket. A muted 2.19% gain after a 9.43% gap is a near-miss on exhaustion; the risk of a gap fill into negative territory was real and not hedged.

thesis: Top previous-day gainer (+8.26% close-to-open). Rule-based control: buying the prior session's strongest movers with no further filter.
outcome_notes: CIEN went essentially nowhere intraday despite the large prior-day gap — the entry was made into an exhausted move, and the stock spent the session consolidating rather than continuing. The near-zero P&L on a high-priced name signals the gap had fully absorbed available demand before the open.
risks_observed: At ~$554 per share, CIEN concentrates notional exposure in very few shares, amplifying the dollar impact of any adverse tick. This was the clearest case in today's basket where the no-filter rule led to a stale entry; a volume or relative-strength filter at open would likely have avoided this name entirely.

thesis: Top previous-day gainer (+8.01% close-to-open). Rule-based control: buying the prior session's strongest movers with no further filter.
outcome_notes: LSCC extended strongly after its prior-day gap, with 7% of additional intraday gain suggesting the underlying catalyst (likely an earnings beat or design-win announcement) continued to attract buyers through the session. The scheduled exit worked well here as there was no meaningful intraday pullback to stop out on.
risks_observed: Paired with IPGP in the semiconductor space, LSCC adds to sector concentration that represents two of the five positions — a sudden sector-wide de-rating (macro tariff news, a large-cap semi miss) would have clipped both simultaneously. The basket finished 4-for-5 today, but the lack of any stop across all five names means a bad macro session could have reversed all positions before the scheduled close.

thesis: RSI 26.1 with price ~3 ATRs below the 20-day MA ($21.65 vs $16.92), volume 1.48× average, and zero negative news — a textbook technical oversell with no story-driven reason for the decline. Targeting partial reversion toward the 20-day MA over 5 sessions.
outcome_notes: Price recovered directionally from $16.52 to $17.08, confirming the technical oversell read — no news emerged to explain the prior decline, and buyers stepped in as expected. However, exit at $17.08 leaves price still ~$4.50 below the 20-day MA, meaning the 5-session window expired well before the reversion target was approached; the thesis held but the timeframe underdelivered.
risks_observed: A 3-ATR gap from the MA on a name this far below fair value likely requires more than 5 sessions to mean-revert; the scheduled exit systematically caps the upside on the deepest dislocations. Thin liquidity in mid-cap healthcare names like EYE can also slow reversion if sector rotation isn't supportive.

thesis: RSI 24.9 with price ~4 ATRs below the 20-day MA ($20.72 vs $16.00) and absolutely no news driving the -17% 5-day decline — pure technical selloff in Energizer Holdings, strong mean reversion setup.
outcome_notes: Clean reversion from $16.00 to $17.84 with no competing news narrative — the 4-ATR compression plus no-news filter produced the sharpest result in the day's basket. Price still sat below the 20-day MA at exit, so the move was genuine early-stage reversion rather than an overshoot.
risks_observed: The -17% 5-day decline preceding entry never had an identified catalyst, which is a latent risk: if a delayed fundamental driver (guidance cut, channel check) surfaces post-entry it would invalidate the 'pure technical' framing retroactively. Consumer staples names with modest float can also face exit slippage if the recovery loses momentum intraday at the scheduled close.

thesis: RSI 25.8 deeply oversold with four sell-side analysts (Canaccord, BMO, Truist, JPM) all maintaining bullish ratings — the decline is target-cut-driven, not thesis-broken; consensus price targets of $730–875 vs $630 provide a strong institutional floor for mean reversion.
outcome_notes: Price continued lower to $622.65 — the analyst-floor thesis failed to hold within the 5-session window, suggesting target-cut-driven institutional rebalancing was still in progress at entry. Bullish analyst ratings and high consensus targets are a lagging signal when sell-side price-target revisions are actively cascading.
risks_observed: High-coverage large-cap biotech is a structurally poor fit for a 5-session mean-reversion window: analyst-driven selloffs in names like REGN often resolve over weeks as funds remodel, not days. The correlation between multiple banks cutting targets simultaneously signals systematic repositioning that can overwhelm RSI oversold signals; this setup class warrants a category-level filter or a longer hold allowance.

thesis: RSI 25.1 with price ~4 ATRs below the 20-day MA ($19.25 vs $14.71) and no fundamental news to justify the -30% 20-day decline — Portfolio Recovery Associates experiencing a purely technical selloff with strong reversion potential.
outcome_notes: Recovered from $14.46 to $15.38 on schedule with no news emerging to justify the prior decline, confirming the purely technical read. The 6.4% gain is solid but price remained deeply depressed versus the 20-day MA, consistent with a reversion that started but didn't complete in the allotted window.
risks_observed: A -30% 20-day decline without an identifiable catalyst in a debt-collection name is a yellow flag: consumer credit cycle exposure and regulatory risk (CFPB, state-level debt collection rules) can produce slow-bleed declines that look like technical selloffs but are fundamentally driven. If macro credit stress is the silent driver, 5-session reversion is structurally unlikely regardless of RSI depth, and the thesis should require an explicit 'no macro deterioration' check.

thesis: RSI 19.7 is the most extreme oversold reading in the entire candidate set; no fundamental news explains the -33% 20-day decline, suggesting capitulation selling. Small allocation acknowledges yesterday's stop hit; tight stop at -6% limits downside if decline continues.
outcome_notes: The RSI 19.7 capitulation signal proved accurate — price snapped back 9.1% to $30.22, validating the re-entry after the prior session's stop-out. The combination of extreme oversold reading and no fundamental catalyst produced the fastest and cleanest reversion in the basket.
risks_observed: Two entries in the same name on consecutive sessions (stop-out followed by re-entry) doubles the sequencing risk: a second stop-out would have compounded the loss and signalled a genuine trend, not noise. Building-products/home-efficiency exposure concentrates the portfolio in rate-sensitive sectors, so if the -33% decline had a macro housing-data driver, the recovery seen here could easily reverse on the next Fed communication.

thesis: EXV3.DE is the unambiguous sector leader: 5d +4.18% / 20d +8.77%, a 3.29x volume surge confirming institutional participation, RSI 66.9 (strong momentum, not yet extended), and the energy supply-shock macro regime showing no reversal signal. Two consecutive winning sessions validate the continuation setup; a 2-day hold captures the sector rotation move while wider stops accommodate ETF-level noise.
outcome_notes: Price moved cleanly from entry to the midday take-profit target, a ~9.7% gain captured in a short hold — consistent with the continuation thesis playing out without reversal. The midday exit suggests the move accelerated intraday rather than grinding over the full two-day window, which indicates the institutional volume surge at entry was a genuine catalyst, not noise. No stop-out or thesis failure; the exit was discretionary profit-taking, not forced.
risks_observed: A single-name ETF on a European energy index concentrates sector and FX risk simultaneously — EUR/GBP movement could have eroded nominal GBP P&L even on a correct directional call. RSI near 67 at entry left limited cushion before overbought territory; a broader energy sector reversal intraday (e.g. oil headlines) could have flipped the position before the take-profit triggered. No trailing stop or partial-exit ladder was noted, meaning the full position was exposed to a snap reversal right up to the exit point.

thesis: Best setup in the set: fresh earnings beat with profit upgrade drives a 14.6% 5-day run while RSI 64.7 and above-average volume signal the trend is still healthy, not overextended. Earnings continuation is the cleanest momentum catalyst available today.
outcome_notes: Price drifted up by a single tick and was held to the scheduled close, suggesting the intraday momentum was effectively flat after entry — the 14.6% 5-day run had already absorbed most of the earnings catalyst before the position was opened. The exit reason being scheduled rather than a target confirms no meaningful continuation occurred on the day.
risks_observed: Entering late in a multi-day post-earnings run is the core risk here: by the time RSI and volume confirm, the easy money is often gone and the remaining upside is thin. A position this size relative to the move also means transaction costs erode most of the gain, so the effective edge was near-zero.

thesis: The 3.41× volume surge on full-year earnings results is the key differentiator versus recent high-RSI failures — institutional conviction is visible in the tape. MACD firmly positive and both MAs confirmed; tight stop set below today's range to manage RSI 72.8 risk.
outcome_notes: The stock faded from entry through the close despite the volume-backed thesis, indicating the institutional buying flagged in the tape was not sustained intraday — price action reversed the morning strength and the position was carried to a scheduled exit rather than stopped out. The RSI-72.8 risk flagged at entry materialised as a mean-reversion headwind rather than being contained by the 'tight stop' mentioned in the thesis.
risks_observed: The scheduled exit overriding the stated tight stop is the critical failure mode to audit: either the stop was never placed, was too wide to trigger, or was abandoned — any of these undermines the risk management logic. At the basket level, holding two single-day momentum longs into a scheduled close with no dynamic exit on the loser concentrates downside in the weaker name and caps asymmetry on both sides.

thesis: RS Group reported full-year FY2026 earnings today with a 3.41x volume surge, the clearest signal of institutional accumulation on results day. Strong cash flow generation and the 'building momentum' narrative gives the market permission to re-rate; today's session is the primary catalyst window before the story is fully digested.
outcome_notes: Price drifted lower through the session and never reclaimed entry, closing out on the scheduled exit with no recovery attempt. The volume surge on results day appears to have marked distribution rather than accumulation — institutional buyers did not follow through into the close, and the 'building momentum' narrative failed to generate same-day price continuation.
risks_observed: No intraday stop meant the full drawdown was absorbed passively; a trailing stop or time-based cut would have reduced the loss. Earnings-day volume spikes are ambiguous signals — they can represent two-way institutional activity rather than directional conviction. Entering on results day creates binary exposure: if the move is already priced by open, there is limited upside and a full session of potential mean-reversion.

thesis: Currys upgraded FY profit guidance on May 19 with LFL sales +4%, and last earnings surprise was +59.4% — a pattern of consistent beats that analysts will be forced to model. RSI 64.7 leaves room before overbought, and sell-side target price revisions typically arrive the day after a retail profit upgrade, extending the move into Day 2.
outcome_notes: Price drifted cleanly from 1.44 to 1.47, consistent with continued post-upgrade momentum rather than a sharp catalyst spike. The exit was scheduled rather than signal-driven, so it's ambiguous whether the anticipated analyst target-price revision actually arrived intraday or whether the move was simply residual buying from the May 19 announcement. No reversal before exit — the directional call held.
risks_observed: Scheduled exit severs any feedback loop on whether the analyst revision catalyst materialised, making it hard to distinguish thesis validation from coincidental drift. A time-based exit also leaves upside on the table if the revision cycle extended into Day 2 or Day 3 as originally hypothesised. At the basket level, a single UK consumer-discretionary name with no paired short means any broad retail sector reversal — e.g., a weak consumer confidence print — carried unhedged downside.

thesis: Corvex Management's public call for a Whitbread sale (May 18) establishes a live M&A premium — activist campaigns of this type typically sustain elevated pricing as long as no deal is rejected. Stock remains above both SMAs with RSI 54.7, and the story is likely to receive additional press coverage today, supporting a continued bid.
outcome_notes: The stock edged slightly higher as expected, but the gross gain was insufficient to clear transaction costs, producing a net loss despite correct directional call. The absence of a meaningful intraday move suggests the Corvex catalyst had already been substantially absorbed in the days prior to entry.
risks_observed: Activist M&A campaigns re-rate quickly on initial press; entering three days after the Corvex announcement likely meant buying into an already-priced premium with little incremental catalyst remaining for the session. Holding two news-driven trades simultaneously (earnings + M&A) on the same day concentrates the book around the shared 'catalyst already digested' failure mode — both positions essentially faced the same risk that the news was stale by entry.

thesis: Top previous-day gainer (+6.28% close-to-open). Rule-based control: buying the prior session's strongest movers with no further filter.
outcome_notes: Price ground higher through the session without any meaningful reversal, and the scheduled exit captured a clean continuation. The level held from open, suggesting the prior-session catalyst was still being absorbed by buyers rather than faded by sellers.
risks_observed: No stop-loss was active, so the full downside was open had the move reversed intraday — the positive result here is partly fortune. As the largest prior-day mover in the basket, SGRO.L carried the highest mean-reversion risk of the five names.

thesis: Top previous-day gainer (+5.31% close-to-open). Rule-based control: buying the prior session's strongest movers with no further filter.
outcome_notes: Price was essentially flat from open to scheduled exit, with no directional conviction in either direction. The session-level move had already been fully priced in before entry, leaving nothing to capture intraday.
risks_observed: A near-zero gross return still produced a net loss once costs were applied, illustrating that trades with no intraday edge are reliably value-destructive. Capital was fully committed with no stop, so any modest intraday dip would have been held through to exit regardless.

thesis: Top previous-day gainer (+4.57% close-to-open). Rule-based control: buying the prior session's strongest movers with no further filter.
outcome_notes: Price sold off steadily from the open and offered no recovery before the scheduled exit, with the session closing near its low. The open level attracted sellers, not buyers — a clean reversal of the prior session's strength.
risks_observed: The absence of any stop-loss meant the full drawdown was absorbed mechanically; this is the clearest case in today's basket where a trailing stop or time-based stop-loss would have materially reduced damage. Three of five names in the basket closed in the red today, suggesting correlated mean-reversion pressure across the UK small-cap universe that the strategy has no mechanism to detect.

thesis: Top previous-day gainer (+4.39% close-to-open). Rule-based control: buying the prior session's strongest movers with no further filter.
outcome_notes: Price moved fractionally in the right direction intraday, but the gross gain was entirely consumed by transaction costs, producing a net loss despite a correct directional call. The move was too shallow to be economically meaningful.
risks_observed: The gap between positive price return and negative net P&L highlights that thin-edge continuation setups are structurally vulnerable to spread and commission drag. Without a minimum expected-return threshold, this strategy will systematically produce trades where the cost structure exceeds the available edge.

thesis: Top previous-day gainer (+4.38% close-to-open). Rule-based control: buying the prior session's strongest movers with no further filter.
outcome_notes: Price drifted lower from the open with no intraday recovery and closed below entry at the scheduled exit. There was no identifiable catalyst to sustain the prior session's level, and the name simply faded through the day.
risks_observed: Like SAGA.L, the purely time-based exit with no stop provided no protection as the trade moved against entry. With the majority of basket names reversing today, the strategy is running significant basket-level correlation to a single factor — UK small-cap post-gap mean reversion — with no hedge or circuit-breaker in place.

thesis: Consumer Staples macro alignment (mildly bullish) with fresh high-quality earnings catalyst — 9.5% revenue growth and +18% profit — delivered yesterday, supported by 1.24x volume confirmation and RSI 60 (not overbought) above both SMAs. Cranswick's volume-led growth and capex commitment are exactly what the defensive rotation thesis calls for.
outcome_notes: Price drifted steadily upward from entry and held the gain through the scheduled close — the earnings catalyst absorbed sellers without any notable intraday reversal. Exit was mechanical rather than signal-driven, so the trade captured only a slice of whatever re-rating the beat is delivering.
risks_observed: Scheduled exit with no trailing structure means upside was capped arbitrarily; if the earnings re-rating has further to run over days, the position was closed too early. CWK.L and DGE.L in the same basket created back-to-back Consumer Staples concentration — a single sector rotation reversal would have clipped both simultaneously.

thesis: Admiral Group (insurance) sits in the Financials sector rated mildly bullish in today's cross-asset snapshot, and insurers specifically benefit from elevated rate environment via investment income — RSI 63.2 is not overbought, MACD positive histogram, and +8.76% 5d trend is intact above both SMAs with clean risk/reward.
outcome_notes: Price followed the established 5-day trend without interruption and the scheduled exit captured the continuation cleanly. No intraday dislocation suggests the macro and technical alignment were genuinely in sync on the day.
risks_observed: Entering after a +8.76% 5-day run means the position absorbed meaningful momentum risk — a mean-reversion session would have turned the setup against the thesis quickly with no stop in place. Admiral's investment-income sensitivity means any surprise dovish repricing of rates intraday (e.g. unexpected data print) could have unwound the thesis faster than a scheduled exit would have caught.

thesis: Diageo sits squarely in Consumer Staples (mildly bullish macro), with a new CEO opening a US$415M Alabama production facility signalling operational confidence; RSI 63.7 and positive MACD above both SMAs provide a clean technical setup for continuation of the week's +6% move.
outcome_notes: Price moved only fractionally, insufficient to cover execution costs — the week's +6% momentum had stalled and the CEO/facility catalyst was largely priced in by entry. The scheduled exit exited a degraded position rather than a live thesis.
risks_observed: Entering a name already up 6% on the week with no incremental fresh catalyst on the day itself was the key failure mode — the signal was backward-looking by the time of entry. The pairing with CWK.L means the basket carried pure Consumer Staples concentration, with no offsetting sector; a defensive-rotation unwind would have hit both legs at once.

thesis: XLF is the #2 sector by 5-day return with a clean hold above both SMAs and RSI at a neutral 52; the Iran truce/oil-drop news shifts the session risk-on and financials are the primary beneficiary, with the structural yield-curve steepening (3m/10y at +105bp) providing a durable NIM tailwind through the 2-day hold window.
outcome_notes: The Iran truce thesis materialized as expected — risk-on conditions did develop — but XLF failed to convert that macro tailwind into meaningful price appreciation over the hold window, delivering only a token +0.09% USD move. FX drag on the GBP-denominated book then turned that small win into a net loss, suggesting the alpha was already priced in at entry.
risks_observed: Unhedged GBP/USD exposure is silently eroding edge on USD ETF positions: a trade that closed green in the underlying still booked a GBP loss, and this will systematically understate or reverse returns in sterling-weakening environments. The scheduled exit also left no room to capture any delayed follow-through had the risk-on rotation extended into the next session.

thesis: XLV shows the strongest MACD histogram inflection of any sector today (+0.420 vs prior -0.554 signal), confirming a momentum cross while RSI sits at a neutral 54 above both SMAs; healthcare's insensitivity to the Iran truce macro shift makes it a clean technical long with defined risk.
outcome_notes: XLV drifted steadily higher from entry to exit, delivering a modest but clean gain consistent with the momentum setup. The MACD cross held and price never threatened the entry level, suggesting the technical read was correct even if the move lacked conviction. Exit was scheduled rather than signal-driven, so no deterioration in thesis was observed intraday.
risks_observed: A 0.70% gain on a scheduled exit leaves open whether the momentum signal had more to give or was already exhausting — no trailing stop or signal-based exit was in place to discriminate. Healthcare's defensive character muted both upside and downside, making this a low-risk but low-information trade that tells you little about the strategy's edge in more volatile conditions. Single-sector concentration in XLV with no offsetting position means any surprise macro catalyst (e.g. drug pricing news) would have had no hedge.

thesis: Phase 3 TRIUMPH-1 topline data released this morning shows retatrutide (GLP-1/GIP/glucagon triple agonist) met all primary and key secondary endpoints at 80 weeks — the largest potential obesity drug catalyst since tirzepatide approval. Fresh today, not yet absorbed by institutional buyers who will need to update 12-month models.
outcome_notes: Price advanced steadily from entry and held gains through the scheduled exit, confirming that the TRIUMPH-1 data was still being absorbed rather than fully priced. The move was orderly rather than gap-and-fade, consistent with institutional buyers building positions through the session. Exiting on schedule rather than a momentum target suggests the re-rating was still incomplete at close.
risks_observed: At ~$1,028 per share, a modest adverse move carries outsized absolute-dollar exposure relative to position sizing; any FDA or reimbursement commentary (even tangential) could have overwhelmed the data catalyst intraday. Pharma catalysts on Phase 3 readouts also carry residual data-interpretation risk — a single bearish sell-side note on secondary endpoints could have reversed early buyers before scheduled exit.

thesis: AMD announced $10B+ Taiwan partnership commitment and 2nm EPYC Venice ramp for Helios Rack-Scale AI platforms today, delivering concrete AI capex evidence the day after Nvidia's beat validated the infrastructure spend cycle. Stock is flat on the 5-day despite the 20-day run, meaning the news hasn't been digested yet.
outcome_notes: Stop triggered with price falling roughly $12 from entry, invalidating the 'not yet digested' thesis almost immediately. The most likely mechanism was a classic coattail reversal: after Nvidia's beat the prior day, AMD latecomers were already long, the Taiwan partnership was treated as a cost commitment rather than a near-term revenue catalyst, and marginal buyers rotated back into Nvidia directly.
risks_observed: Entering AMD as a second-order Nvidia beneficiary the day after Nvidia's blowout created asymmetric timing risk — the primary beneficiary had already absorbed the institutional flow, leaving AMD exposed to profit-taking with no independent catalyst strong enough to replace it. ARM and AMD held simultaneously produced semiconductor concentration; a sector-wide de-rating (which is what appears to have happened to AMD) risked both legs at once.

thesis: Nvidia's earnings beat directly validates ARM's royalty revenue outlook as every data-center Nvidia chip runs on ARM IP; Bernstein $300 target (17% above current) and pre-market +3% continuation confirm institutional buyers are still accumulating into the agentic AI chip demand upgrade.
outcome_notes: ARM was the strongest performer in the basket, moving nearly to the Bernstein $300 target before the scheduled exit. The royalty-leverage-to-AI-volumes thesis was the cleanest re-rating story of the four trades and attracted sustained buying through the session rather than a fade after the open. Scheduled exit captured the bulk of the single-day catalyst move.
risks_observed: Entry followed a pre-market +3% move, meaning some of the catalyst was already priced and the position was exposed to a gap-fill reversal if NVDA's intraday action turned cautious. ARM's extreme P/E multiple means any softening of AI capex language — even in a different earnings call — compresses the multiple faster than it expanded; the upside captured here could unwind on a single macro headline.

thesis: Raymond James upgrade to Outperform with $55 price target — 58% above current $34.81 — arrived yesterday with 2.26× volume and remains the freshest analyst catalyst in the energy sector; SM's recent debt paydown and +37.8% prior earnings beat provide fundamental support for the bullish re-rating.
outcome_notes: Stop triggered after the stock failed to hold the initial upgrade pop; entry at $35.11 was already above the prior close of ~$34.81, meaning early momentum buyers had front-run the position and there was no residual demand to absorb their exits. Energy stocks are primarily driven by commodity price, not sell-side opinion, so the absence of a constructive oil tape left the upgrade catalyst structurally thin.
risks_observed: A 58% gap between current price and the analyst target signals the upgrade originated from a deeply sceptical base rather than a momentum inflection, which limits buy-side credibility and urgency to act. Holding SM alongside three technology/pharma names meant this trade had no sector correlation hedge — if the broader basket was right-skewed on risk, SM's energy exposure added idiosyncratic downside with no offsetting relationship to the other positions.

thesis: Energy sector is the macro regime's strongest confirmed bid — XLE +5.77% 20d and supply-shock thesis intact. MPC is the highest-quality expression: Goldman raises PT, record US refined product exports at 7.92m b/d, high refinery utilisation, and RSI 61.9 (not overbought) with clean technical structure above both SMAs.
outcome_notes: MPC declined steadily through the holding period and was exited at the scheduled close with no intraday catalyst to reverse it. The Goldman PT raise and export-volume data were already priced in or insufficient to drive near-term momentum; sector-level XLE strength did not translate to single-stock price appreciation over this window.
risks_observed: No stop on a directional large-cap energy name meant the full drawdown was realized without truncation — the scheduled exit structure provided no downside protection. Combined with WMB, the basket carried two energy or energy-adjacent names that both lost on the same day, revealing meaningful sector concentration even though MPC and WMB were positioned as distinct expressions.

thesis: Consumer Staples is the macro view's second pillar — defensive rotation confirmed with XLP +4.15% 20d. COST is the cleanest expression: new all-time high, UBS raises to $1275, and the direct mechanism (higher gas prices driving traffic to fuel-station anchored warehouses) means the stagflationary macro is a structural tailwind, not just sentiment.
outcome_notes: The stop was triggered, confirming a sharp enough reversal from entry to breach the downside level. Buying into a fresh all-time high on an analyst upgrade is an extended entry; when the broader tape offered no follow-through, mean-reversion from that level moved quickly enough to take out the stop before any recovery.
risks_observed: Entering at an all-time high compresses the distance to any rational stop, making the trade mechanically fragile to even modest reversals — the stop did its job but the setup accepted that risk structurally. The fuel-station traffic mechanism is a multi-month thesis layered onto a stock already pricing in significant optimism, which creates a mismatch between catalyst time horizon and the single-day holding window.

thesis: Midstream natural gas infrastructure diversifies energy exposure away from crude-price Iran headline risk while staying in the bullish energy sector. Morgan Stanley raises PT to $98 (+26% upside) on Overweight — a fresh and specific catalyst on a fee-based business model that insulates from spot oil swings.
outcome_notes: WMB drifted lower and exited at the scheduled close; the Morgan Stanley upgrade and fee-based insulation narrative generated no near-term buying interest sufficient to hold the entry price. The diversification rationale versus crude-price risk did not prevent the name from moving in the same direction as the rest of the energy basket.
risks_observed: The supposed decorrelation from spot oil via fee-based revenues didn't manifest on the day — WMB and MPC both declined, suggesting that on short horizons midstream names still carry substantial correlated energy-sector beta. Two scheduled exits in the same session with no stops on either energy name amplified the realized loss versus what a trailing stop or tighter exit structure would have allowed.

thesis: Upstream E&P exposure completes the energy stack (refiner + midstream + E&P). Citigroup raises PT to $147 with EOG above both SMAs and a healthy RSI 58.7; 2-day hold keeps the horizon short enough to exit before any Iran resolution fully re-prices crude.
outcome_notes: Price drifted lower through the hold and never reclaimed entry, suggesting the Citi upgrade was already priced in or failed to attract incremental buyers within the 2-day window. The scheduled exit captured the loss cleanly with no adverse gap, but the analyst catalyst produced no measurable lift — crude price action was the dominant governor, not the PT revision.
risks_observed: Running refiner, midstream, and E&P simultaneously concentrates the book in a single commodity driver; a crude leg-down hits all three in the same direction with no natural offset. The Iran-resolution tail risk flagged at entry — the very reason for the short horizon — may have weighed on E&P sentiment even without a formal announcement, and there was no stop in place to limit downside if the diplomatic newsflow accelerated mid-hold.

thesis: Nvidia earnings confirmed $2B surge in agentic AI chip demand with ARM architecture at the center — Bernstein $300 PT and +3% premarket gap signal institutional buying pressure continuing intraday. Strongest momentum name in the candidate set with volume confirmation.
outcome_notes: The Nvidia spillover thesis held intraday — price moved cleanly toward the Bernstein $300 PT with no meaningful reversion, confirming institutional follow-through rather than a fade. Scheduled exit captured the bulk of the move; there was no adverse price action that warranted an early close.
risks_observed: The trade was entirely dependent on a single macro catalyst (Nvidia earnings read-through), leaving it exposed to any intraday narrative reversal in semiconductors. The scheduled exit structure left no mechanism to extend the hold had momentum continued — and with the $300 PT still overhead at close, that was a real opportunity cost.

thesis: Back-to-back analyst upgrades (BTIG $76, Oppenheimer Outperform $85) on the same day as 5d +12.46% momentum creates a fresh catalyst that can extend the move — cybersecurity's defensive positioning buffers against tech macro headwinds.
outcome_notes: The analyst upgrade catalyst did not generate fresh buying — price drifted lower from entry, consistent with the upgrades being already absorbed into the prior 5-day run. Scheduled exit meant the position held through the full session with no mechanism to cut early.
risks_observed: Entering a name up 12%+ in five days on analyst upgrades is structurally a buy-the-news setup where the easy money is likely behind; there were no intraday signals at entry that new demand was arriving. The absence of a trailing stop or hard stop converted what should have been a defined-risk trade into a slow bleed to close — correlated with ARM in the AI/tech complex, the basket also lacked sector diversification.

thesis: Goldman Sachs PT raise to $207 (+15% upside) lands directly on a macro regime where US refiners are running at multi-year utilization highs with record product exports — energy sector leadership + analyst upgrade is a durable 2-day catalyst.
outcome_notes: The analyst upgrade failed to act as a near-term price catalyst — PSX sold off through the stop without any recovery attempt, suggesting the Goldman PT raise was either already priced in or overwhelmed by short-term headwinds in refining margins or crude spreads. The "2-day catalyst" window never opened; price moved directionally against the thesis from the outset.
risks_observed: Analyst PT raises are a weak momentum trigger in energy names where crack-spread volatility and macro sentiment regularly dominate single-stock news flow. A stop placed 2.9% below entry left limited room for noise in a sector with intraday ranges that can easily exceed that threshold, and there was no volume or technical confirmation that accumulation was actually underway at entry.

thesis: MACD histogram +19.757 is the most powerful building-momentum signal in the candidate set, paired with 5d +15.55% and strong volume — B of A maintaining Buy with $1400 PT provides a 14% upside anchor supporting continued institutional accumulation.
outcome_notes: The scheduled exit captured a clean continuation of the pre-existing momentum — price advanced steadily from entry without requiring stop management, consistent with institutional accumulation absorbing supply. The MACD signal held its predictive value for the duration of the hold window.
risks_observed: Entering after a 15.5% five-day run means a meaningful portion of the move was already behind; any negative surprise during the hold (guidance cut, macro risk-off) would have faced little technical support between entry and a distant stop. At this price point, a single high-conviction name dominates basket notional, and correlation with broad tech sentiment is a tail risk the BofA PT anchor does nothing to hedge.

thesis: Top previous-day gainer (+998.00% close-to-open). Rule-based control: buying the prior session's strongest movers with no further filter.
outcome_notes: Residual retail momentum from the prior session's extreme move carried ELOX upward through the day, and the scheduled close captured a clean gain. Price action held the entry level without a significant reversal, suggesting selling pressure hadn't yet exhausted by open. Exit timing was fortunate — no intraday stop was needed.
risks_observed: A sub-$1 stock following a near-tenfold prior-day move is prone to violent mean reversion; this trade benefited from timing luck rather than any structural edge. No intraday stop left the full position exposed to a washout that didn't materialise.

thesis: Top previous-day gainer (+550.00% close-to-open). Rule-based control: buying the prior session's strongest movers with no further filter.
outcome_notes: GOEVQ carries a 'Q' OTC suffix indicating active bankruptcy proceedings; it trades in sub-penny fractions. Entry and exit both recorded at $0.00, so the entire loss is pure bid-ask spread and execution cost on an effectively illiquid instrument — no directional movement occurred.
risks_observed: Buying a bankrupt OTC stock at sub-penny prices means the spread alone constitutes a double-digit percentage cost per round trip; the strategy had no filter to exclude securities in insolvency. This is a structural flaw, not a market-condition risk.

thesis: Top previous-day gainer (+400.00% close-to-open). Rule-based control: buying the prior session's strongest movers with no further filter.
outcome_notes: ADAPY traded at $0.01 round-trip with no net price movement; the loss is entirely bid-ask spread on an illiquid ADR with negligible float. The prior-day percentage gain was a nominal artifact of the low absolute price, not a signal of genuine demand.
risks_observed: At $0.01, a single tick is a 100% price move, making spread losses guaranteed on any round trip without a substantial directional run. The strategy has no minimum price or liquidity filter to screen out instruments where spread cost exceeds any realistic intraday gain.

thesis: Top previous-day gainer (+300.00% close-to-open). Rule-based control: buying the prior session's strongest movers with no further filter.
outcome_notes: TIOG also traded flat at $0.01 entry and exit; the loss is spread and execution friction on a sub-penny-tier instrument. The +300% prior-day figure reflects penny-stock arithmetic rather than real institutional or retail demand that would carry forward.
risks_observed: Same structural issue as ADAPY — no price floor filter means the strategy routinely enters instruments where the minimum tick width makes profitable exits near-impossible. Collectively, ADAPY, TIOG, GOEVQ, and BIORQ represent concentrated exposure to the same failure mode within a single session.

thesis: Top previous-day gainer (+200.00% close-to-open). Rule-based control: buying the prior session's strongest movers with no further filter.
outcome_notes: BIORQ is a bankrupt issuer ('Q' suffix) trading at sub-penny prices. Entry and exit at $0.00 with a £971.80 loss implies an enormous share count was acquired, with the entire position value consumed by spread on a stock with near-zero liquidity and no realistic exit market.
risks_observed: This is the single largest loss in the basket and the clearest failure case: the strategy allocated significant capital into a bankrupt, sub-penny security where spread cost is structurally total. The absence of position-sizing guardrails relative to instrument liquidity and the lack of any bankruptcy/delisting screen are the critical gaps this trade exposes.

thesis: Munich Re is 2.21 ATRs below its 20-day SMA with RSI 34.7, and the 5-day return already turning positive (+1.92%) signals that aggressive sellers are exhausting — no negative news to justify the 14.6% 20-day decline. Lower FX-only cost gate means predicted +1.5% over two sessions clears the threshold with room to spare.
outcome_notes: The entry price recorded as $0.00 is a data capture failure — any cost-gate or sizing calculation made against it was meaningless. The scheduled exit at €409.12 with a small loss indicates Munich Re continued to drift rather than snap back toward the SMA within the holding window; the positive 5-day momentum signal did not sustain, likely overwhelmed by ongoing institutional de-risking in European insurers.
risks_observed: The $0.00 entry record exposes a critical gap: if the fill price is not validated at order confirmation, the entire pre-trade edge calculation is built on bad data. EUR/GBP translation adds a second noise layer when P&L is reported in GBP, masking whether the loss was price action or FX drift.

thesis: RSI 35.8 and 1.86 ATRs below SMA20 with no stock-specific negative news (the Motherson article covers an Indian supplier, not BMW); the low FX-only cost gate means +1.0% clears the 1-day bar. Shorter hold is appropriate given MACD histogram still deteriorating — take the oversold bounce without assuming multi-day follow-through.
outcome_notes: Price drifted marginally lower from entry to exit, with no meaningful bounce materialising despite the oversold setup. The anticipated mean-reversion catalyst never arrived within the hold window, and the scheduled exit captured a small loss rather than the expected +1.0% recovery — suggesting the oversold condition deepened or simply flatlined rather than snapping back.
risks_observed: The deteriorating MACD histogram flagged at entry was a live warning that downside momentum hadn't exhausted; holding through a scheduled exit with no stop loss meant the position had uncapped intraday downside if sentiment worsened. Broader European auto sector weakness or EUR/GBP moves could have amplified the loss without any stock-specific trigger, and the low FX-only cost gate may be too permissive for entries where momentum indicators remain bearish.

thesis: Healthcare is macro-aligned as a defensive play in today's risk-off session (Nvidia miss + hawkish central banks); LLY.DE adds a stock-specific catalyst with Phase 3 retatrutide showing 28.3% weight loss and the Engage Biologics acquisition extending the pipeline, creating a genuine re-rating event on top of the sector defensive bid. Two-day hold allows full price discovery on news published after yesterday's close.
outcome_notes: Price moved steadily through the session and held gains into the scheduled close, suggesting the defensive bid was real and the retatrutide news continued to find buyers rather than fading intraday. The scheduled exit captured the move cleanly — no evidence of a stop hunt or mean-reversion that would have argued for an earlier exit.
risks_observed: EUR/GBP translation drag was a latent headwind throughout; a weaker euro on the day would have meaningfully compressed the sterling return. Clinical-stage re-rating events can reverse sharply on analyst downgrades or secondary data reads, and the two-day hold window left no dynamic exit mechanism if sentiment shifted overnight.

thesis: Energy is the strongest macro sector and oil holds above $100 on Hormuz geopolitical premium with Iran talks unresolved; Repsol adds a stock-specific bid via Pikka Alaska Phase 1 production startup, and its FX-only 0.30% round-trip cost structure means the cost gate is cleared at materially lower returns than stamp-duty LSE energy names, improving the risk/reward ratio.
outcome_notes: The oil macro backdrop held but Repsol moved against the trade regardless, implying the stock was responding to something other than spot price — likely European refining margin compression or general Spain/EM equity outflows on the risk-off day. The scheduled exit enforced a full hold through a losing position rather than allowing a cut when the stock diverged from the sector early in the session.
risks_observed: Holding energy equity as an oil proxy in a risk-off session is structurally inconsistent — equities carry balance-sheet and sentiment risk that crude futures don't, and that gap widened here. The Pikka startup catalyst was likely stale at entry (production news already circulating), so the stock-specific kicker that was supposed to offset sector noise wasn't fresh enough to generate incremental buyers.

thesis: Direct crude oil exposure in the highest-conviction macro sector; above-average volume (1.48x) alongside healthy RSI 59.5 and positive MACD histogram confirms institutional rather than retail participation, and oil holding above $100 on Hormuz premium provides a natural intraday support floor. One-day hold keeps the cost gate at +1.00%, which the energy thesis comfortably clears.
outcome_notes: Price drifted 0.75% lower from entry and was closed at the scheduled end-of-day exit with no intervening stop or target trigger. The volume and momentum signals did not translate into intraday follow-through, suggesting the Hormuz-premium bid had already been absorbed before entry rather than providing a continuing tailwind. Exiting on schedule rather than on price action means the strategy accepted the full drift loss passively.
risks_observed: A time-based exit is a blunt instrument on a momentum entry: once the thesis stopped working intraday there was no mechanism to exit early, so the position simply bled to close. CRUP.L as a single-name crude proxy carries basis risk — stock-specific factors (e.g. fund flows, spread widening) can decouple it from spot oil regardless of the macro backdrop. The +1.00% cost gate cited in the thesis left very little margin for any adverse move before the trade was offside.

thesis: Trump administration's $1 billion quantum foundry grant to IBM, announced today (2026-05-22), is a fresh hard-dollar government catalyst with immediate repricing implications. Volume at 2.37× the 20-day average confirms institutional buying is already underway; 1-day hold captures the event-day move before the news is fully digested.
outcome_notes: The quantum grant failed to produce sustained intraday repricing — price sold off from entry through the scheduled exit, suggesting the catalyst was either front-run before the open or dismissed as a long-dated, non-revenue event. Volume confirmation at entry did not persist into buying pressure; the 2.37× spike likely reflected opening-auction noise rather than durable institutional accumulation.
risks_observed: Government R&D grants carry optionality-style value that markets often discount steeply on day one, making them poor 1-day catalysts relative to revenue or earnings surprises. IBM.DE as a German-listed wrapper adds intraday EUR/USD drag that compounds against a falling underlying. No intraday stop meant the full drawdown was absorbed rather than cut when the thesis failed to materialize within the first hour.

thesis: Phase 3 retatrutide data showing up to 28.3% weight loss over 80 weeks is a major pipeline upgrade for Eli Lilly's obesity franchise; the low cost gate (0.30%) gives ample margin versus the expected move, and healthcare is insulated from today's central-bank and China macro headwinds.
outcome_notes: Price moved in the expected direction and held through the scheduled exit, consistent with the Phase 3 readout being a genuine pipeline upgrade rather than a pre-leaked or already-priced event. The healthcare sector's macro insulation held on the day, removing a common headwind that affected other sectors.
risks_observed: Phase 3 weight-loss data carries binary read-through risk — a miss or safety signal would have produced a sharp reversal well beyond the 0.30% cost gate, and a scheduled exit offers no protection in that scenario. Both legs of today's basket are German-listed wrappers of US-domiciled names, meaning correlated EUR/USD exposure sits unhedged across the book; on a day with USD strength, that drag would have clipped both positions simultaneously.

thesis: Rheinmetall's Q1 2026 earnings beat (sales €1,938m vs prior-year €1,800m, net income up) continues to drive institutional re-rating with RSI at 39.7 well below overbought levels; NATO spending tailwinds provide structural support for a 2-day post-results drift continuation below both key moving averages.
outcome_notes: T212 paper portfolio was reset on 2026-06-01 (platform-level reset by user). Position was force-cleared in the ledger because the broker-side state was wiped; no real fill price was captured. Treat P&L as missing for evaluation.
risks_observed: Real fill price not captured because the platform reset preceded the close.

thesis: Top previous-day gainer (+35.14% close-to-open). Rule-based control: buying the prior session's strongest movers with no further filter.
outcome_notes: Price held flat from entry to scheduled close; no follow-through on the prior-session gap. The thesis that momentum would continue intraday did not materialise — the move had already fully resolved before the open. Net loss is purely transaction cost.
risks_observed: Penny-stock spread risk is acute at £0.20: a single tick is a meaningful percentage of entry, and any fill slippage absorbs the entire expected edge. Four of five positions in today's basket shared this flat-gap-fade pattern, suggesting the prior-gainer signal has low intraday predictive value at this price tier.

thesis: Top previous-day gainer (+30.00% close-to-open). Rule-based control: buying the prior session's strongest movers with no further filter.
outcome_notes: No intraday price movement from entry to scheduled exit; the +30% close-to-open gap did not extend. The position contributed nothing beyond absorbing transaction costs, consistent with a fully-digested overnight event.
risks_observed: Cross-listed or thinly-traded Paris-listed micro-caps carry FX conversion costs on top of spread, which amplifies the drag on flat trades (£-12.09 vs £-10.00 for the London equivalents). Currency exposure was unhedged and added noise to an already zero-alpha day.

thesis: Top previous-day gainer (+27.27% close-to-open). Rule-based control: buying the prior session's strongest movers with no further filter.
outcome_notes: Price was unchanged from entry to scheduled exit; the prior-session +27% gain saw zero continuation. The trade was effectively a flat carry, with the entire P&L being transaction cost.
risks_observed: BEM.L at £0.07 is at the extreme low end of tradeable price, where minimum-tick moves represent double-digit percentage swings and spread cost alone can exceed the position's daily range. At this price level the strategy is taking maximum spread risk for minimum directional opportunity.

Macro backdrop explicitly supports semiconductors via unbroken AI capex narrative and yield pullback tailwind; stop placed at -10% (just below 1 ATR) to allow intraday noise room given the ETF's structural volatility.

The thesis that momentum would extend after a +51% 5-day run did not hold; buying into a near-vertical move made the position immediately vulnerable to any mean-reversion trigger. Critically, the stated -10% stop was not the actual exit — the scheduled close was, meaning the position was held ~4 percentage points through the intended stop level with no intervention.
risks_observed: The stop either was not wired up, was overridden by the scheduled-exit logic, or gapped through without fill — whichever the case, a core safety net failed, and the loss exceeded the pre-defined maximum. Entering a 3x levered instrument as the *sole* candidate in the basket means zero diversification and no offsetting exposure to absorb the drawdown; a single bad day in semis produced the full portfolio hit. Entering after a +51% 5-day run on a leveraged ETF carries implicit mean-reversion and volatility-decay risk that the RSI-below-70 filter does not capture.

thesis: Financials sector Neutral with yield-curve NIM tailwind intact (97bp spread) and benign credit; DBK shows the cleanest MACD histogram expansion (+0.219) in the European bank group on a +8.83% 5d run, and the 0.30% round-trip cost means only 0.60% predicted return needed to clear the gate.

thesis: UK short gilts are above both SMAs with a bullish MACD histogram and RSI 62, aligned with the week's yield pullback (10Y eased to 4.49%, 30Y to 5.03%); a 2-day hold is essential to sidestep the single-session scheduled-exit trap that erased the 2026-05-19 return before any directional move could materialise.

thesis: RSI 35.5 with MACD histogram just turning positive (+0.099) after a -4.5% 20-day decline places Fresenius ~1.46 ATRs below the 20-day SMA at €39.87 with no fundamental bad news — cleanest technical mean-reversion setup today. thesis: RSI 36.6 with MACD histogram inflecting positive after an -8.64% 20-day decline places Danone ~3.1% below its 20-day SMA with no news catalyst; predicted 1-day bounce of ~1.3% clears the elevated French FTT cost gate (1.05%) with a tight stop to cap downside in a risk-off scenario.

French FTT friction compressed the effective edge on smaller size, and a single-name staples position on a risk-off day carried sector rotation risk that didn't materialise but was not hedged.

thesis: Base metals are the cleanest setup in the complex today — DBB is above both SMAs with RSI 61.3 and the strongest 5d/20d momentum across all candidates. Single-ETF concentration in base metals with no hedge against a broader risk-off rotation.

thesis: Spire Global signed an MoU with Schaeffler AG today (May 27) to develop space hardware subsystems and satellite platforms — a company-specific revenue-visibility catalyst in the satellite internet mainstreaming theme. SPIR and AAL both shared the satellite internet theme and both hit stops on the same day, meaning thematic concentration across two concurrent positions amplified basket drawdown.

thesis: American Airlines' confirmed Starlink deal for 500 narrowbody planes (announced May 26, still being absorbed at 1.79x volume) plus UBS Buy rating with $18 PT vs $14.85 close provides a 21% fundamental anchor. The satellite internet mainstreaming theme is the dominant sector narrative today, supporting continuation.

The catalyst was a May 26 announcement entered on May 27, meaning at least one full session of price discovery had already occurred before the position was opened.

Combined with SPIR sharing the same thematic narrative, the basket carried two correlated satellite-theme stops on a single day, a concentration risk that was not bounded at the portfolio level.

thesis: IREN's $1.6B Blackwell hardware agreement with Dell published today adds fresh AI infrastructure revenue visibility in the session before tomorrow's earnings. A 1-day hold exits before the earnings announcement, capturing pre-earnings enthusiasm; last earnings surprise was +10.7%, keeping institutional buyers engaged.

The £-4.60 loss on zero price movement is purely transaction cost, flagging that the alpha window had likely closed before entry and the risk/reward was negative in expectation.

thesis: XLK is the undisputed sector leader — Nasdaq 100 at record 30,000+, semiconductor ETF +4.8% yesterday, and 20d rel-strength vs SPY at +10.46% dwarfs every other sector. Single-sector concentration in XLK means any macro shock (rates, tariffs, earnings miss from a mega-cap constituent) hits the full position with no offset elsewhere in the basket.

thesis: Healthcare is forming a fresh MACD bullish cross (histogram +0.613 against still-negative signal at -0.141), is above both SMAs with RSI 58 leaving room to run, and carries the macro view's highest-conviction long rating; 1-day hold captures the technical setup while keeping cost gate manageable.

Healthcare sector ETFs can stall on any macro health-policy headline, and holding a single sector ETF with no hedge means the full sector drawdown risk was live throughout.

thesis: Top previous-day gainer (+7293.62% close-to-open). Rule-based control: buying the prior session's strongest movers with no further filter.

risks_observed: A gain of that magnitude almost always reflects a low-float, thinly traded name where the gap is phantom or illusory by the time a market order executes. No circuit-breaker or minimum-float filter means this class of 'gainer' will reliably appear in the scan and reliably deliver nothing.

thesis: Top previous-day gainer (+2400.00% close-to-open). Rule-based control: buying the prior session's strongest movers with no further filter.
outcome_notes: GOEVQ carries the 'Q' suffix denoting active bankruptcy proceedings; the $0.00 price reflects a sub-cent instrument where fills, spreads, and fees consume the entire position. The 2400% reported gain was illiquid noise with no executable move.

The £-62.58 loss on a 0.00% price change is entirely a transaction-cost artefact, making this the largest absolute drag in the basket despite being a 'control' position with no discretionary input.

thesis: Top previous-day gainer (+1400.00% close-to-open). Rule-based control: buying the prior session's strongest movers with no further filter.

thesis: Top previous-day gainer (+1175.00% close-to-open). Rule-based control: buying the prior session's strongest movers with no further filter.

Concentration risk here is in the screener logic itself, not sector or factor.

thesis: Top previous-day gainer (+800.00% close-to-open). Rule-based control: buying the prior session's strongest movers with no further filter.

Basket-level correlation here is total — every single trade failed via the same mechanism, which makes the control strategy's daily drawdown structurally predictable and unbounded without a stop-loss.

thesis: IG credit is outperforming HY this week (-0.24pp HY-IG diff), confirming the market prefers defensive credit quality in this transitional late-cycle regime; LQD is the cleanest expression — above SMA20, positive MACD histogram, and a direct beneficiary of the continued 10Y yield decline to 4.48%.

thesis: Technology sector (XLK, Mildly Bullish macro); semiconductor equipment structurally benefits from the AI capex build-out as TSMC, Samsung, and Micron expand capacity. thesis: DBB is the only commodity ETF above both its 20d and 50d SMA with RSI momentum still above 60; the dollar's failure to break 100 eliminates the primary cross-asset headwind, and the macro view's residual growth optimism (DBB +3.46% 20d) supports the copper/aluminum complex. risks_observed: Single-name commodity ETF with no intraday stop meant the full drawdown was absorbed passively — a trailing stop at entry or a modest intraday exit trigger would have reduced the loss. The one-day hold discipline was correctly applied given thin volume, but the position still carried full notional exposure into a session where the underlying metals complex lacked a catalyst, making the risk/reward asymmetric from the open.

thesis: Top previous-day gainer (+30.50% close-to-open). Rule-based control: buying the prior session's strongest movers with no further filter.

thesis: Top previous-day gainer (+25.67% close-to-open). Rule-based control: buying the prior session's strongest movers with no further filter.
